title: Quality Sentinel: Estimating Label Quality and Errors in Medical Segmentation Datasets
mechanism: Regressor on (image, label) predicts the label's Dice against a correct label, trained on synthetic corruptions; used to pick high-quality labels and pseudo-labels.
adaptation: Train on 532 labelled cells with EL-specific corruptions (1-3 px shifts, width 1-4 px, dropped/spurious segments, inactive boundary errors), target relF1@2 and inactive IoU; use to rank train labels and to select pool pseudo-labels image by image.
min_experiment: Arm: house + top 1,000 pool cells by predicted pseudo-label quality (5-seed teacher). Baseline: house and earlier pool SSL. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: predicted-vs-true quality Spearman < 0.5 on real val labels, or no gain over earlier pool run.
evidence: R: r = 0.902 between predicted and true label Dice over 142 structures; 4M training pairs; quality-selected pseudo-labels gave 33-88% gain over entropy selection; 1/3 annotation cost cut on TotalSegmentator.
prior_overlap: Pseudo-label SSL row: per-pixel hard/tolerant thresholds with 11.9k pool at 100% labels n.d.; image-level learned quality selection not run. Partly open.
